core_meaning.primary_meaning: Abdullah (عبد الله, ʿAbd Allāh) is a two-part Arabic name: ʿabd (“servant”) followed by Allāh (“Allah/God”). Together it means “servant of Allah.” The construction expresses devotion and should be distinguished from a claim that the proper name is a standalone Qur’anic title.

faq.a: Abdullah (عبد الله) means “servant of Allah,” combining ʿabd (“servant”) and Allah.

faq.q: How is Abdullah formed in Arabic?
faq.a: It is an iḍāfa construction: عَبْدُ اللهِ (ʿabdu llāh), a noun followed by its genitive complement.
Yes. Abdullah is an Arabic compound name, written عبد الله.

faq.q: Does the phrase ʿabd Allāh occur in the Qur’an?
faq.a: The phrase “servant of Allah” occurs in Qur’anic Arabic. That should be distinguished from identifying every occurrence as a reference to someone whose proper name is Abdullah.

faq.q: Why is Abdullah used in Muslim communities?
faq.a: Its meaning expresses servitude to Allah, an important concept in Islamic belief and devotional language.

faq.q: What does Abdullah mean in Urdu?
faq.a: It is written عبداللہ or عبد الله and means “اللہ کا بندہ” — servant of Allah.
A practical English guide is “ab-dul-LAH”; Arabic pronunciation joins the two elements closely.
Not exactly. “Worshipper” is a direct gloss for ʿābid (عابد); Abdullah specifically means “servant of Allah.”
